title: Elon Musk on Dwarkesh: Limiting factors, urgency, and hiring for hard-tech companies
summary: Long Dwarkesh interview covering space-based AI compute, chips, robots and politics. The durable business lessons are Musk's operating method: always attack the current limiting factor, set aggressive 50th-percentile deadlines, run detailed engineering reviews, and hire for talent, drive and trustworthiness rather than resumes.

principles.text: Always find and attack the single limiting factor; spend your time where it gates progress.
principles.quote: Yeah, I'm constantly addressing the limiting factor.

principles.text: Set the most aggressive deadline you think has a 50% chance of being hit; schedules expand to fill the time given.
principles.quote: the most aggressive deadline I can think of that could be achieved with 50% probability.

principles.text: A maniacal sense of urgency from the leader propagates through the whole company.
principles.quote: I have like a maniacal sense of urgency.

principles.text: Hire for talent, drive and trustworthiness; domain knowledge can be added later but those traits cannot be changed.
principles.quote: I think it's a good idea to hire for um, uh, talent and drive and trustworthiness.

principles.text: Trust the live conversation over the resume when evaluating candidates.
principles.quote: don't look at the resume just believe your interaction.

principles.text: Take drastic action only when you conclude success is otherwise impossible.
principles.quote: only when I conclude that um success is not in a set of possible outcomes.
